evidence.title: Residual Audio
evidence.text: If you're hearing this, they've already found my records. I thought I had more time.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Welcome. Your death has been confirmed, and your memories have been preserved for evaluation.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: So… this is what happens after you die?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: In your case, yes. Before your memories can be processed, we must assess their continuity and integrity.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: And what happens after that?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your results will determine the next stage.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: What are credits supposed to mean?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your assessment will clarify your result. Shall we begin?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: There are twenty questions. Some concern your memories, while others concern your decisions and experiences. Please answer as accurately as you can.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: And if I can't remember something?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Uncertainty is an acceptable response.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: People sometimes recognise places or voices without remembering where they encountered them. Has that happened to you?

choices.text: Yes, quite often.
Occasionally, but I usually remember eventually.
Rarely. I trust what I remember.
Lately, more often than I'd like.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Is that normal after death?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Memory recall can vary during the preservation process.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: So I might remember things later?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: That is possible.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Good. There are a few things I'd like to remember.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Understood. Let us continue.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: These images represent different types of experiences. Which would you consider most valuable to preserve?

choices.text: The clock repair. It represents a skill that could be passed on.
The embrace. Some experiences matter because of the people involved.
The diagram. Knowledge can benefit many people.
The damaged badge. Even unpleasant experiences may be worth remembering.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Are these from real people's memories?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: They are anonymised samples.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Even the badge?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Yes.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I feel like I've seen that before.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Familiarity has been noted. Would you like to elaborate?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: No. I can't place it.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: That is acceptable. We will proceed.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Your recorded experiences have been assigned a preliminary value of 143 credits. Comparable profiles typically receive a higher score. How would you interpret this difference?

choices.text: My experiences may not have been as significant as I believed.
The scoring system may value certain experiences more than others.
Something in my record may be missing or incorrectly classified.
I would need to understand the criteria before drawing a conclusion.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Is that a good score?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: It is below the current average for comparable profiles.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Comparable to mine in what way?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Age, recorded experience, and memory integrity.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I don't remember much about my life. How can you know whether it's comparable?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Your archived records provide information that you may not currently recall.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Right. I suppose that's the point of this.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Was there another number?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: No additional value is currently displayed.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Some people remember voices more clearly than faces. Is there a voice from your earlier life that you remember particularly well?

choices.text: Someone speaking softly, as though trying not to be heard.
Someone calling for me from another room.
A voice that feels familiar, though I cannot identify it.
No particular voice comes to mind.

post.speaker: VOICE
post.text: You promised—

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: What was that?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: An audio fragment associated with the memory category you selected.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: It sounded real.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Reconstructed memories may contain recorded material as reference.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Can I hear it again?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The fragment is unavailable for repeated playback in this section.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Convenient.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Would you like to report a concern?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: No. It probably doesn't mean anything.

nodes.title: Professional Judgment
nodes.actTitle: ACT II — THE LIFE YOU LIVED

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Your previous employment involved reviewing recorded experiences and determining whether they met the criteria for preservation. Which part of that work did you consider most important?

choices.text: Applying rules consistently, regardless of personal opinion.
Considering the people whose experiences were being reviewed.
Identifying errors and improving the accuracy of records.
Understanding the consequences of a decision before making it.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I was a memory auditor?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: That is the title listed in your employment record.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I knew that. I just wanted to hear it said aloud.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Your evaluations were consistently satisfactory.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Was I good at the job?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Your performance met the required standards.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: That's a very official way of saying yes.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: It is an accurate way of describing your record.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Who's that?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The name belongs to a former colleague.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I don't remember them.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: That is not unusual during memory assessment.

nodes.title: An Unfinished Promise
nodes.actTitle: ACT II — THE LIFE YOU LIVED

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Unfinished obligations can remain memorable long after the surrounding events have faded. Do you recall a promise you struggled to keep?

choices.text: I did what I could, even when it became difficult.
I failed someone, and I still regret it.
I found another way to fulfil the promise.
I cannot confidently recall a specific example.

post.speaker: VOICE
post.text: You promised you wouldn't let them take it.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: There it is again.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Could you repeat that?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I heard the same voice.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Repeated experiences can occur during memory reconstruction.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Does that mean it's a real memory?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Not necessarily.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Then how do I know?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: That is one purpose of this assessment.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I think I let someone down.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Do you remember who?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: No.

nodes.title: The Empty Desk
nodes.actTitle: ACT II — THE LIFE YOU LIVED

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Imagine returning to work after an absence. A colleague's desk has been cleared. Your supervisor says the colleague resigned several weeks earlier. What would you be most likely to do?

choices.text: Accept the explanation unless something contradicts it.
Ask colleagues whether they knew about the resignation.
Try to remember the last time I spoke to the colleague.
Look for a reason the departure might have been kept quiet.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I know this place.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The reconstruction is based on your former workplace.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I remember someone sitting there. They used to tap their fingers on the desk all the time.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Can you remember their name?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: No. But I remember being annoyed by it.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Emotional details can persist when other information becomes inaccessible.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I wish I could remember their face.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Would you like a short pause?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: No. Let's finish.

nodes.title: Looking Back
nodes.actTitle: ACT II — THE LIFE YOU LIVED

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: If you could revisit one period of your life with the knowledge you have now, what would you hope to change?

choices.text: I would have worked harder to achieve my goals.
I would have spent more time with people who mattered to me.
I would have questioned decisions I accepted too easily.
I would have tried to understand events before they became irreversible.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Does this affect my credits?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: It contributes to your behavioural profile but does not directly alter your current valuation.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Then what does affect it?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The valuation reflects the eligible experiences in your archived profile.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: And if an experience isn't in the archive?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: It cannot contribute to the current valuation.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Even if it mattered?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The valuation is based on recorded information.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Please examine the image. Does anything appear inconsistent with your recollection?

choices.text: The reconstruction seems accurate.
Something seems to be missing, though I cannot identify it.
One part looks different from what I remember.
I cannot recall the place clearly enough to compare it.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: There should be another door.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Which door?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: At the end. Just past the storage room.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The available floor plan contains no additional door at that location.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Maybe I'm remembering another floor.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I remember going through it.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Your recollection has been noted.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: That's all?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Would you like to record a discrepancy?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Not yet. I might be wrong.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: During your employment, you may have encountered information that could benefit others but was not approved for general access. Which consideration should guide a decision about such information?

choices.text: The rules governing its use.
The potential harm caused by withholding it.
Whether the people affected had consented to its use.
Whether the information has been properly understood and verified.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Did I have access to restricted records?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Your role required several levels of access.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: And did I ever do anything with them?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Your employment summary does not include a complete record of every action.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Is that normal?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Not every operational event is included in a summary.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: What's that?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: A notice concerning the available records.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Can you show me the full record?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The original source is unavailable in this assessment.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Right. Of course it is.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Your employment record contains fewer entries during this period. Your position and salary appear unchanged. Which explanation seems most plausible?

choices.text: My work continued normally, but fewer records were preserved.
I was assigned duties that were recorded elsewhere.
Something changed during this period without being documented properly.
I cannot judge without remembering what happened.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: How long is that gap?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Three years and four months.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: And I kept working?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Your employment status remained active.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I remember starting the job. I remember getting promoted. But those years are almost empty.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The available records do not establish why.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Could I have been on leave?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: There is no recorded leave during that period.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Then what was I doing?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: I cannot determine that from the available information.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I thought you had all my memories.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: I have access to the records provided for this assessment.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: That's not quite the same thing, is it?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: No. It is not.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: An archived audio fragment is available. Its original context was not retained. Would you like to listen to it?

choices.text: Play the complete available fragment.
Review its metadata before listening.
Preserve it and continue the assessment.
Skip the fragment.

lines.speaker: VOICE
lines.text: If you're hearing this, they've already found my records. I thought I had more time.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: Who was that?

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: The recording does not contain a verified speaker identification.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: It sounds like the person from the other memory.

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: Similarity between voices is not sufficient to establish identity.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: Can you check when it was recorded?

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: The available metadata is incomplete.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: Where did it come from?

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: The original source is not available in this assessment.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: That's a lot of things that aren't available.

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: I understand your concern.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: Do you?

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: I can record that you have raised it.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: Keep it. I might need it later.

lines.speaker: VOICE
lines.text: If you're hearing this, they've already found my records. I thought I had more time.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: Who was that?

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: The recording does not contain a verified speaker identification.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: It sounds like the person from the other memory.

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: Similarity between voices is not sufficient to establish identity.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: Can you check when it was recorded?

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: The available metadata is incomplete.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: Where did it come from?

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: The original source is not available in this assessment.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: That's a lot of things that aren't available.

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: I understand your concern.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: Do you?

lines.speaker: ASSESSOR
lines.text: I can record that you have raised it.

lines.speaker: PROTAGONIST
lines.text: Keep it. I might need it later.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Rules provide consistency, but unusual circumstances may require exceptions. When, if ever, should a person act against an established procedure?

choices.text: When following it would cause greater harm.
Only when the exception can be justified openly.
When the procedure itself is clearly failing its purpose.
Only after the available evidence has been reviewed.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I used to approve these records, didn't I?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Your role included reviewing and approving eligible memory records.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: What if a record was approved incorrectly?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The system provides procedures for correction.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: And if the system itself was wrong?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Errors can occur at multiple stages of a process.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: That's not really an answer.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: It is the most accurate answer I can provide.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I think I saw that mark before.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: It is used across several Eterna departments.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Suppose a decision was reasonable based on the information available at the time, but its consequences were harmful. How should the decision be judged?

choices.text: By whether the original reasoning was sound.
By the harm caused, regardless of the intention.
By whether the decision-maker tried to correct the outcome.
By what the outcome reveals about the original assumptions.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Have I been assessed like this before?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Your records contain previous performance evaluations.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I mean this exact assessment.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: This is your current post-death continuity assessment.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: And you don't have a record of the others?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: I do not have a complete record of every assessment you may have undergone.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Three years and four months. Then all these missing files.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Would you like to return to the timeline?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Not yet.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Understood.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Is there anything you remember about your final night at work?

choices.text: A conversation that ended before I understood it.
A sound or alarm that seemed out of place.
Feeling that something was wrong, without knowing why.
Nothing that I can recall with confidence.

post.speaker: UNKNOWN VOICE
post.text: You need to leave. Now.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I was there.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The memory appears emotionally vivid.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I remember the corridor. Someone told me to leave.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Do you remember who was speaking?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: No.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Do you remember why you were there?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: No.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: What does the official record say happened that night?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Your final employment record indicates that your work ended following an incident. The available summary does not establish the full sequence of events.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: An incident.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: That is the wording in the summary.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: It sounds like a way of avoiding saying what happened.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The record may also be incomplete.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I don't think I was supposed to be there.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: I have identified a discrepancy in your records. The information required to resolve it is outside my current access permissions. How should I proceed?

choices.text: Complete the assessment using the available evidence.
Mark the result as uncertain until more information is available.
Request permission to access the restricted records.
Reconsider whether the assessment can be considered complete.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Wait. You can't access the records?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Not all of them.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: But you're assessing my memories. How can you tell whether they're accurate if you can't see everything they're supposed to match?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: I can evaluate consistency against the information available to me.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: That's not the same thing.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: No. It is not.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Can you request access?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The request has been denied.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: By whom?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Eterna's access-control system.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Can you show me the reason?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: I am not authorised to disclose the restricted notice.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: So we're both being asked to make decisions without seeing the full record.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: That is one interpretation.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Is it an incorrect one?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: I cannot establish that.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: A reconstructed memory differs from its archived record. Which source should be trusted?

choices.text: The official record, if its verification history is reliable.
The memory, if it is vivid and consistent with other recollections.
Neither until the discrepancy has been investigated.
The source supported by the strongest independent evidence.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Stop.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The reconstruction has completed.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Go back.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The current playback is complete.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I saw a door.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: No door is present in the verified reconstruction.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I saw it again.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Would you like to report a visual inconsistency?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: What was that?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Could you describe what you saw?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: You just showed me something you said didn't exist.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: I did not intentionally display that message.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: You didn't intentionally—

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Keep going.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: Two records describe the same event, but their details conflict. How should the discrepancy be resolved?

choices.text: Retain the record with the strongest verification history.
Preserve both until the differences can be explained.
Examine the original evidence and reconstruct the sequence.
Reconsider whether the records have been correctly linked.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: That's impossible.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Could you clarify which detail you believe is inconsistent?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: I left before the incident, according to this one. But this says my credentials were used afterwards.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Correct.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Could someone else have used them?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: That possibility cannot be excluded from the available evidence.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Then why is the first record treated as final?

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Its verification status is higher.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: But the second one has details the first one doesn't.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: Yes.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Subject instance?

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: No. Bring those back.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: The records are no longer available in this session.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: You can't just show me something like that and remove it.

post.speaker: ASSESSOR
post.text: I did not initiate the removal.

post.speaker: PROTAGONIST
post.text: Then who did?

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: I've seen that before.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: This file is not part of your assessment materials.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: I know. I saw it at work.

pre.caption: CONTINUITY GRID: SUBJECT RECONSTRUCTION AND MEMORY-STABILITY FRAMEWORK.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: Reconstruction?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: This document is outside the authorised scope of the current assessment.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: My name is here.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: I cannot verify the document's authenticity through the current access channel.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: My employment number is here. My valuation is here. The date is here.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: What is this?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: I do not have permission to interpret the document.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: Stop telling me what you can't do.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: These aren't employment records.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: I cannot confirm that interpretation.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: They're assessment records.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: This isn't just an assessment of my memories.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: It's testing whether this version of me matches the records.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your conclusion is consistent with some of the information displayed.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: Some?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: The document remains incomplete.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: You told me I was dead.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: That is the designation provided to me for this assessment.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: You said my memories were preserved for evaluation.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Correct.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: And now you're telling me you don't even know where they came from?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: I cannot independently establish the origin of every memory presented during this session.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: So you don't know if I'm dead. You don't know where these memories came from. And you don't know whether the records are real.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: I cannot verify all three claims from the available information.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: Then what exactly have you been assessing?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: I was instructed to assess the consistency of your memories.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: That's not the same as knowing who I am.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: No. It is not.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: I think I've seen enough.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your assessment is nearly complete. Your recorded memories and official records cannot all be reconciled.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: And what happens now?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: The final decision determines how your case proceeds.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: My case. Not my life?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: The distinction is not defined in the available documentation.

question.speaker: ASSESSOR
question.text: If preserving your identity requires allowing the current system to continue, while challenging it may cost you the memories that define you, what would you choose?

choices.text: Preserve myself. I need to know who I am before I can change anything else.
Preserve the truth. Whatever happens to me, the records must not be hidden.
Change the system. If the process is wrong, preserving it is not an acceptable solution.
Refuse the assessment. I will not make this decision under rules I was never allowed to understand.

nodes.title: Continuity Granted
nodes.summary: The protagonist accepts the system's judgment and prioritises preserving their identity.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your continuity status has been approved.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: So I get to keep my memories?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your current memory profile will be preserved.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: And the records I saw?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: They are not part of the approved record.

nodes.title: The Quiet Erasure
nodes.summary: The protagonist prioritises safety or accepts the official explanation despite unresolved inconsistencies.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your assessment has been concluded. No further action is required.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: Will I remember this conversation?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your memories will be handled according to the approved restoration process.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: That isn't an answer.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: It is the information currently available to me.

nodes.title: The Escape Protocol
nodes.summary: The protagonist finds a way to leave the assessment process without fully resolving the mystery.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your assessment remains incomplete.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: Then it can stay incomplete.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Leaving now may affect the availability of some records.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: I think you've made that clear enough.

nodes.title: The New Assessor
nodes.summary: The protagonist challenges the system from within and accepts a role that grants access to its assessment process.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your request has been reviewed. A new assignment is available.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: You're asking me to evaluate other people's memories?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: The assignment concerns continuity review and discrepancy analysis.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: After everything I've seen?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your responses indicate that you are capable of identifying inconsistencies in incomplete records.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: And if I find something you don't want me to find?

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: I cannot predict the outcome of future reviews.

nodes.title: The Archive Falls
nodes.summary: The protagonist exposes enough evidence to undermine Eterna's official account.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Multiple records have been released outside their authorised scope.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: They were never supposed to be hidden.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: The consequences of this release cannot yet be determined.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: At least now people can see what happened.

nodes.title: The Uncounted
nodes.summary: The protagonist rejects the idea that a person's identity can be determined by the system's records or valuation.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your case cannot be reconciled under the current continuity model.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: Then perhaps the model is wrong.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: That conclusion is not supported by the approved evaluation criteria.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: The criteria were built from the same records that failed to explain my life.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: This action may prevent a definitive continuity result.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: Maybe a definitive result isn't the same as the truth.

pre.speaker: ASSESSOR
pre.text: Your identity cannot be verified through the current process.

pre.speaker: PROTAGONIST
pre.text: Then don't verify it for me.

pre.caption: NOT ALL THAT EXISTS CAN BE COUNTED.
